newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weak as market awaits U.S. rate news.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weak as market awaits U.S. rate news.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended sharply lower on Friday as investors remained cautious ahead of a much-awaited decision on U.S. interest rates next Tuesday, analyts and delaers said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended 13.05 points lower at 1,212.94, while the all-share EMAS index was off 3.89 to 355.28.

"The fear of a U.S. rate hike is very real. If there were any potential buyers out there, they would be waiting until next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting," said Teoh Kok Lin, head of research at HSBC James Capel in Kuala Lumpur.

The most active stock of the day was Selangor Dredging, with 49 million shares traded, acounting for roughly 13 percent of total market volume. The stock was up 17 cents to 2.57 ringgit. Company officials could not be reached for comment on the activity.

United Engineers fell 60 cents to 21.70. The company reported a net profit of 513 million ringgit for the year to December 31, 1996 on Thursday. Some analysts had forecast the result would be as high as 580 million ringgit.
"This is probably a good time to be buying stocks," said Amerjit Chinna, an analyst at equity research house BZW.
